HFIP-Promoted Friedel−Crafts Allenylation of Imidazopyridines with
Propargyl Alcohols at Room Temperature
Srinivasarao Yaragorla,* Aayesha Shaik, and Dandugula Sneha Latha

ABSTRACT: Herein, we report an efficient synthetic protocol for the Friedel−Crafts reaction of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines with
propargyl alcohols in HFIP. Notably, this FC allenylation works without any additional solvent or catalyst and requires neither inert
conditions nor heating. In this method, HFIP, besides offering hydrogen bonding with propargyl alcohol, also stabilizes the resultant
carbocation, thus forming the product. This method also enables the straightforward synthesis of 1,3-enynes. The current method
offers a large substrate diversity with good to excellent yields. We also demonstrated gram-scale synthesis and synthetic
modifications.
■
INTRODUCTION
Among the diverse range of nitrogen-containing privileged
heterocycles, imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines occupied a special place
in synthetic organic and medicinal chemistry due to their rich
presence as natural products and pharmaceuticals.
1
The
derivatives of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines exhibit a broad range
of biological activities including, antiulcer,

that contain the imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine as the
core moiety (Figure 1). Besides, these molecules are important
in the preparation of polymer films due to their significant
fluorescent properties.
9
Subsequently, the synthesis and
derivatization of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines, in particular, C3-
functionalization, received an overwhelming response from
many research groups, toward the development of C−H
alkylation, arylation, aroyl methylation, hydroxy-alkylation,
thio-carbamation, aminomethylation, sulfonylation, thio-cyan-
ation, selenization, halogenation, amination, trifluoromethyla-
tion, sulfenylation, carbonylation, selenocyanation and many
more.
10,11
Apparently, electrophilic aromatic substitution, and,
in particular, Friedel−Crafts alkylation or acylation, is probably
one of the most recurrent tools used to derivatize imidazo[1,2-
a]pyridines using conventional metal-catalyzed strategies. For
example, Hajra and coworkers reported the FC reaction of
imidazopyridines and propargyl alcohols by refluxing them in
toluene at 110 °C for 16 h with Zn(OTf)
2
as the catalyst.
12
On the other hand, 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol
(HFIP), the magic solvent, proved to be an excellent promoter
system in organic synthesis, particularly for the carbon−carbon
bond formation reactions.
13
Although the role of HFIP is
initially realized in stabilizing the cationic intermediates,

14
HFIP facilitates electrophilic aromatic substitution
reactions due to its peculiar properties, such as higher polarity,
increased Brønsted acidity, high ionizing power, low
nucleophilicity, and strong hydrogen-bond donation proper-
ties. Therefore, a number of investigators have studied FC
alkylation chemistry in HFIP. For example, Cativiela et al.
reported that FC alkylation product 3-(2-furyl)-propanal was
formed as a byproduct during the Diels−Alder reactions of
furan and acrolein in HFIP.
15
Subsequently, a few more
elegant approaches toward FC alkylations have been reported
from allylic alcohols,
16
epoxides,
17
and benzyl halides,
18
intramolecular benzoylation,
19
acylation,
20

hols,

23

24

25
in HFIP (Scheme 1).
Recently, we reported FC-arylation of various α-imino
ketones and subjected them to cyclization to obtain 2-aryl
pyrroles and 2-aryl indoles.
26
We also demonstrated that HFIP
can promote the ring-opening cyclization of DA-cyclopropanes
to obtain 2,3-dihydro pyrroles and benzimidazoles.
27a,b
Later, a
mechanochemical approach for the formal [3 + 3] cyclization
of various enaminones with propargyl alcohols was also
developed with HFIP.
27c
Given the importance of the FC
reactions in HFIP, we sought to develop the allenylation of
imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines with propargyl alcohols in the
presence of HFIP and report our initial results here.
■
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
To investigate the FC reaction conditions, we chose propargyl
alcohol (1a) and imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine (2a) as the suitable
reacting partners (Table 1). Initially, a mixture of 1a (0.52
mmol), 2a (0.63 mmol) and 5/5 mol % Ca(OTf)
2
/Bu
4
NPF
6
was stirred in HFIP at room temperature for 24 h and to our
delight, we observed the desired product was formed in less
than 76% (entry 1, Table 1). Increasing the catalyst loading
was undesirable as there was no improvement in the yield
(entry 2). To check the role of HFIP, we performed the
reaction without HFIP and realized that the product was
formed in a trace (entry 3). This indicated that the HFIP solely
promoted the reaction. Hence, we performed the reactions
with HFIP, by varying its volume from 0.1 to 0.3 mL and
finally, 0.5 mL was found to be excellent for yielding 3a in 93%
within 15 min at room temperature (entries 4−6).
Having the optimum reaction conditions in hand, we then
switched to studying the generality of the FC reaction. As
showcased in Scheme 2, initially, we studied the scope of
various propargyl alcohols in the FC reaction of imidazo[1,2-

a]pyridine (2a). Under the standard conditions, propargyl
alcohols, 1a to 1p, furnished the corresponding products 3a to
3p in excellent yields. These examples illustrate that electronic
and steric factors on propargyl alcohols did not remarkably
influence product yields. This method allowed the synthesis of
not only tetra aryl allenes but also alkyl-substituted allenes
(3j−3l, 3ad). Next, we turned our focus to studying the scope
of substitutions on the pyridine ring of 2 and synthesized the
corresponding allenes 3q−3s in good yields. The substitutions
on the benzene ring of 2-aryl-imidazo-pyridines were also
found to be less influenced by the electronic effects and
provided the desired compounds (3t−3w) with excellent
yields. Examples 3y to 3ac indicate that the protocol tolerates
the diversity on both the substrates 1 and 2. Further, it is
observed that simple imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine (2y, C2-unsub-
stituted) did not react with 1a under standard conditions for
24 h. When heated to 60 °C (oil bath temperature) for 24 h, a
trace amount of product was observed, which was confirmed
by HRMS data (see Supporting Information). The FC reaction
with other arenes such as furan and pyrrole was not successful
at rt and heating.
As indicated in Scheme 3, oxindole-derived, tert-propargyl
alcohol (4) did not react with 2j under standard reaction
conditions even after 24 h. Heating the reaction mixture at 60
°C was also not desirable as we did not observe any reaction.
Next, sec-propargyl alcohol (5) reacted with 2j and through a
direct FC benzylation to furnish the compound 6 in 85% yield.
Encouraged by these observations, we then switched to
studying the FC reaction of 2 with vinyl propargyl alcohol 7
(Scheme 4). Interestingly, substrate 7 has competitive
functional groups, such as allyl alcohol and propargyl alcohol,
so we can study the chemoselectivity of FC reaction. To our
delight, propargyl alcohol 7a reacted smoothly with various
imidazopyridines in HFIP at room temperature and furnished
the corresponding FC products 8a to 8e in good yields.
Notably, this turned out to be an excellent and simplest
method for the synthesis of 1,3-enynes. Notably, the FC
arylation occurred on allyl alcohol in preference to the
propargyl alcohol via S
N
2′ mechanism. Similarly, 7b and 7c
also reacted with imidazopyridines and furnished the desired
compounds 8f and 8g (Scheme 4). Further, the FC arylation of
these vinyl propargyl alcohols was extended to a different
arene, N,N-dimethyl aniline by treating it with 7d in HFIP at rt
for 30 min, to obtain the desired compound 9 in 87% yield
(Scheme 5).
Having studied the generality of the FC reaction with
various propargyl alcohols, we demonstrated the gram-scale
synthesis of 3a from 1a and 2a and synthesized 1.4 g of 3a
(Scheme 6). Besides, we demonstrated the synthetic potential
of the products by treating 3a with NIS in acetonitrile at rt for
6 h and confirmed that the allene converted into vinyl iodide
10 in 68% yields. Similarly, 3s also furnished the vinyl iodide
11. We have provided the possible route for forming vinyl
iodide from allene. We also reasoned the formation of vinyl
iodides. Notably, the two double bonds of the allene are
distinguished by the higher electron density on the
imidazopyridine-substituted alkene; hence, it underwent cyclic
iodonium formation, followed by the nucleophilic opening
with water furnished the vinyl iodides 10/11 as indicated in
Scheme 6.
After successfully demonstrating the protocol, we proposed
the reaction mechanism for this protocol in Scheme 7. We
believe that the activation of propargyl alcohol 1 with HFIP
proceeds as indicated in structure A to furnish the propargyl
cation B. Isomerization of B to allenyl cation (C) triggers the
electrophilic aromatic substitution (D), (Friedel−Crafts)
reaction to furnish the desired compound 3. Alternatively,
path-b can not be ignored, as the arene 2 can directly react
with activated propargyl alcohol to form 3 via the transition
model (i). In the case of the FC reaction of vinyl-propargyl
alcohol (7) with arene 2, we proposed that the reaction
proceeds as depicted in the model (ii). Likewise, the FC
reaction of sec-propargyl alcohols 5 with 2 may proceed via the
model (iii, Scheme 7).
■
CONCLUSION
In summary, we have developed a highly facile synthetic
protocol for the Friedel−Crafts reaction of imidazopyridine
with various propargyl alcohols in HFIP. We demonstrated
that allenes could be synthesized from imidazopyridine and
tert-propargyl alcohols and alkylation with sec-propargyl
alcohols. Besides, vinyl-propargyl alcohols provided the
efficient synthesis of 1,3-enynes through FC-alkylation. All
these reactions were carried out without any additional catalyst
or solvent. The hydrogen bonding ability and the stabilization
of the carbocation by the HFIP might probably be the key
driving force that facilitates these transformations. The
reaction offers excellent substrate scope and yields. Besides,
we demonstrated the gram scale synthesis and postsynthetic
modifications of the products. We believe that this unique
application for the synthesis of allenes through FC reaction
promoted by HFIP opens up many such novel developments
within its domain of the field.
■
